facility_roles.quote: The CHARMII detector was designed to study neutrino electron scattering. It ran in the CERN SPS neutrino beam.

intervals.label: preparation and setting-up (WA79)
intervals.note: Preparation began in 1983 and the setting-up in 1984 (the archive text reads 'The setting-up started is 1984'); data taking began in 1986. Dore (EPJ H 37, 2012) heads the detector '(1982)'.
intervals.quote: CHARM 2 (Brussels IIHE-CERN-Hamburg-Louvain-Moscow-Munich-Naples-Rome Collaboration) experiments WA79: The preparation of this experiment began in 1983.

intervals.label: data taking (WA79)
intervals.note: The CERN archive gives data taking from 1986 to 12 August 1991. The 1994 Phys. Lett. B abstract analyses 'the CHARM II detector from 1987 till 1991' and the CERN Courier says 'From 1983-91 the WA79 (CHARM II) experiment detected several thousand events'; the archive dates are chosen because they are the experiment's own record of its run.
intervals.quote: The data-taking began in 1986. WA79 was completed on the 12th August 1991.

intervals.label: completed
intervals.note: Terminal event: WA79 'was completed on the 12th August 1991'.
intervals.quote: The data-taking began in 1986. WA79 was completed on the 12th August 1991.

quantity.quote: It was a massive fine grained calorimeter (692 t) of low density (target material glass) followed by a magnetic spectrometer [72].

name: CHARM II
notes: CHARM II (CERN experiment WA79) is a separate collaboration and detector from CHARM (experiment:charm); the CERN Archives file covers both.

physics_goals.quote: The CHARMII detector was designed to study neutrino electron scattering.
physics_goals.value: Study neutrino-electron scattering and determine the electroweak mixing angle free of hadronic-structure uncertainties

summary.plain: A 692-tonne glass-target calorimeter at CERN's SPS built to catch the rare collisions in which a muon neutrino scatters off an electron, a clean way to measure the weak mixing angle. It ran from 1986 to 1991.
summary.technical: CHARM II (WA79): fine-grained low-density calorimeter (692 t, glass target) followed by a magnetic spectrometer in the SPS wide-band nu_mu beam; several thousand nu-e and nu-bar-e elastic events give sin^2 theta_W = 0.2324 +- 0.0083 and the effective couplings g_V = -0.035 +- 0.017, g_A = -0.503 +- 0.017.
